# Market report: 2026-11-27

## Market snapshot
1. **Dow posts its best week since 2022.** In the holiday-shortened Black Friday session the Dow rose 591.99 points (1.2%) to 50,774.94, its steepest weekly climb since October 2022, as battered AI stocks rebounded. Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO drove Monday's surge, and some of that gain has since faded. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/26/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)
2. **Inflation gauge hits 3.8%.** The Fed's preferred inflation measure (PCE) rose 3.8% in the year through October. Core PCE, which excludes food and energy, was 3.3%, the highest since November 2023. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/25/pce-inflation-report-october-2026.html)
3. **A December Fed hike looks likely.** Headlines point to a rate increase at the December meeting after the hot inflation reading. [CNBC (feed link)](https://news.google.?oc=5)
4. **Gold near a 15-month low.** Gold steadied after hitting its lowest level in about 15 months, with rate-hike expectations in focus. [CNBC (feed link)](https://news.google.?oc=5)

## Advisor angle
With inflation at 3.8% and a rate hike likely, an advisor would probably spend client calls on inflation and rates rather than on the one-week stock rebound. That could mean explaining that a big weekly gain doesn't remove rate risk, and reviewing how clients' bond and cash holdings respond to higher rates. This is a planning conversation, not a prediction.

## Term of the day: PCE inflation
PCE (personal consumption expenditures) price index measures how much prices paid by consumers rise over time. The Fed prefers it to some other gauges. "Core" PCE leaves out food and energy, which swing a lot, to show the underlying trend. The Fed's target is 2%.

## Interview talking point
"October PCE inflation came in at 3.8%, with core at 3.3%, so I'm watching how the Fed's December decision shapes the conversations advisors have with clients about rates and inflation."
